messages:
Alex: heads up — eu-west2 GPU attach queue spiking, about 130 pending attaches for the last 5m. noticed high iowait on nodes.
Maria: seeing NVMe metadata errors on several hosts (gnode-eu-12*, gnode-eu-13*). Attach controller is retrying and backing off.
Sahil: logs please — is this read errors or metadata checksum mismatches?
Alex: grabbed dmesg from gnode-eu-12-03, looks like metadata corruption + retry storms.
Alex: ```
[ 1234.567890] nvme0: detected metadata checksum mismatch on namespace 1
[ 1234.568001] nvme-core: requeueing IO due to media error
[ 1235.001234] scrubber: found corrupt extent, scheduling deep-scrub
```
Maria: scrubber ran agressive deep-scrub because of a prior firmware flurry yesterday. concurrent scrub + janitor tempfile sweeps are driving IOPS to 99% and causing attach timeouts.
Sahil: so two problems: (1) underlying NVMe encountered some corrupt metadata, and (2) background maintenance is saturating IOPS and preventing KV cache warmup during attach.
Alex: ops-bot flagged hosts and incremented retry backoff, but we need a short-term mitigation. Can we throttle scrub concurrency and pause janitor in eu-west2?
Maria: I can flip scrubber concurrency to 1 for eu-west2 and pause tempfile sweeps for 10m. that should free some IOPS headroom. doing it now — will post commands.
Maria: ```
# reduce scrub concurrency
kubectl -n storage set env daemonset/scrubber SCRUB_CONCURRENCY=1 --context=prod-eu-west2
# pause janitor cron for eu-west2 pool
kubectl -n janitor patch cronjob/tempfile-sweep -p '{"spec":{"suspend":true}}' --context=prod-eu-west2
```
Sahil: also recommend setting the attach controller to prefer healthy zones for 15m and route surge to dedicated pool if available (to avoid user-facing throttles).
Alex: can we do a canary reroute for new attaches to eu-west1 until nodes recover?
Maria: yes — changing routing policy now to avoid eu-west2 for non-pinned workloads. patching traffic config.
ops-bot: automated note — scrubber concurrency set to 1 on 6 hosts; tempfile-sweep CronJob suspended in eu-west2.
oncall-bot: alert suppressed for 12 minutes for nvme-iops-surge.
Alex: early signal — pending attaches dropped from 130 -> 40 within 90s, CPU and iowait dropping. good.
Sahil: next steps: 1) run single-host deep-verify on the corrupted drives (non-destructive), 2) schedule targeted firmware validation with vendor for the affected cohort, 3) add a transient guard to avoid concurrent deep-scrub + janitor in same AZ.
Maria: filing a follow-up runbook and a small RB to gate scrub concurrency based on current iowait metrics. I'll @infra-oncall in the runbook.
Alex: thanks — keep monitoring. if corrupt extents are increasing we'll retire the affected hosts and reprovision. :thumbsup:
Maria: noted. will update thread with verification results and any host retire decisions.
Sahil: thanks everyone, nice quick mitigation.
